$Comment: Ranger Wren, the Emerald Wilds quest giver, standing beside a Kweebec village.
Anchor.Structure attaches the placement to a worldgen spawn marker rather than to fixed
coordinates, so Wren lands in a village the world actually generated instead of an arbitrary
spot. MarkerIds is an exact, case-insensitive allow-list; run /mmonpc structures in game to see
the marker ids a world has actually loaded before authoring one. The allow-list is FAIL-CLOSED:
a typo means Wren simply never appears.
Limits: one per world, and every matching marker is used (SpawnChance 1 means never skipped).
Raise MaxPerWorld to stand one at every matching village instead.
Identity has no Role, which is what opts this placement into a generated one: the base role is
cloned with the Appearance, the nameplate key and the press-F hint key below, so the pack ships
no role JSON of its own.
Press F opens Wren's dialogue. It is authored as a ui_target rather than as Interact.Dialogue
because that form carries the npc id into the dialogue, which is what Wren's own
'npcquests:@self' options resolve against and what puts the character's name in the header.
Authoring Interact.Dialogue instead would open the same tree with no identity and those options
would go nowhere. The npc id is also what the pack's quests bind as their npcViewId.
Name: Guide_Wilds
